objects.title: ORION model policy: adaptive by difficulty, ceiling Opus
objects.description: The orchestrator picks each agent's model by task/step difficulty via the Agent tool's model param: trivial->haiku, normal->sonnet, hard->opus (ceiling Opus is allowed; floor Haiku). The orion-analyst rates difficulty per sub-objective/step and those ratings drive builder/verifier/fixer model choice; builders run one-per-step so a single plan can mix haiku and opus steps in parallel. Agent frontmatter defaults were set (analyst/planner/builder/verifier/fixer = sonnet, reflector = haiku) so a naive spawn doesn't inherit the main conversation's model. Full rubric lives in the '1b. Model selection' section of ~/.claude/skills/orion/SKILL.md (mirrored in runtime/skills/).
objects.reason: User chose adaptive-by-difficulty with an Opus ceiling. This environment has no live token metering (RFC-0004 budgets are conceptual here), so model choice is the only real cost lever — spending should track difficulty instead of defaulting everything to the most expensive model.

objects.fact: infrapilot-app's next build was failing because the Groq client was instantiated at module scope in app/api/cotizar/route.ts and app/api/licitaciones/analyze/route.ts, causing the build to fail when GROQ_API_KEY was not in the environment. FIXED by moving client instantiation into the request handlers (after the missing key guard) and committed as 5efdde3. Pattern: never instantiate API-key-dependent clients at module scope in Next route files — construct them inside the handler after validating the key is present.

objects.fact: ORION agent hardening for autonomy: all 6 agents (analyst, planner, builder, verifier, fixer, reflector) now enforce single-responsibility boundaries. Builder/fixer cannot commit; analyst/planner/verifier read-only; reflector writes memory only. All agents have hard output caps (e.g., builder max 4000 chars per step, analyst max 3000 per finding). Model policy: haiku for trivial/routine, sonnet for normal, opus for hard tasks (ceiling Opus); planner rates difficulty per step and builder inherits ratings to spawn parallel subagents at appropriate model tier. Reflector baked in AMM schema (no runtime parsing of knowledge-objects.ts); records modelOutcomes per agent spawn (phase, model, verdict) for learning loop.
objects.context: Session 2026-07-02 hardened the ORION ecosystem for continuous autonomy; E2E test passed with zero fix cycles (analyst→planner→builder→verifier→reflector, haiku/sonnet mix).

objects.fact: AMM Schema invariant: tier MUST match lifetime per RFC-0002 §5.2. Tier (Working/Project/Permanent) is a Kubernetes-like cardinality constraint: Working items are Session-scoped; Project items are Sprint/Project lifetime; Permanent items are Permanent lifetime. The validator (tools/validate-memory.mjs) caught real violations in session 2026-07-02: KN-001..005 initially had lifetime=Permanent tier=Project (invalid); repair was KN-001→tier Permanent (machine-level fact justifies permanence); KN-002..005→lifetime Project (facts about infrapilot-app project, not eternal truths). Lesson: future architects must validate tier⟷lifetime pairing on every memory write.
objects.context: Discovered during validation of the E2E pipeline; zero-dep Node.js validator runs offline and caught violations that would have persisted indefinitely if not automated.

objects.title: AMM schema embedded in reflector agent, not runtime-parsed
objects.description: Instead of the reflector loading knowledge-objects.ts at runtime to validate/parse the AMM schema, the schema is baked into the agent's SYSTEM prompt as a table + constraints (LIFETIME_TO_TIER, status values, type-specific fields). This eliminates a runtime TS parser dependency, reduces latency (no file I/O per reflection), and makes the schema version explicit per run (reflector inherits it from its frontmatter at agent load time). If the schema evolves, the reflector's SYSTEM prompt is updated; no AMM-runtime process exists to bump a version field.
objects.reason: Session 2026-07-02 verified that a hand-emulated schema (no live runtime) is viable for ORION's current scale. Baking the schema into the reflector is safer and simpler than attempting to maintain a separate parser binary.

objects.fact: infrapilot-app's tax-by-currency table is hardcoded in lib/utils.ts with standard legal rates: COP and MXN use IVA @19% and @16% respectively; PEN uses IGV @18%; fallback is 'Impuesto' @18%. This branching is correct for the current 3-currency deployment (COP primary), but if InfraPilot expands to additional countries or wants to pull rates from an external source of truth (tax authority APIs, a database, etc.), the helpers (taxLabel(), defaultTaxRate()) must be refactored to consume dynamic configuration instead of literal values.
objects.context: Extracted from PEND-006 F3 (Tax rate mismatch) resolution. The hardcoded rates are intentional and correct per currency, but the pattern (literal switch on currency) is brittle if country coverage expands.

objects.title: Proportional lifecycle: ceremony scales with task size
objects.description: Standing policy (SKILL.md 1d): trivial tasks (1 file, fully specified) run fully inline with zero agent spawns; small tasks (2-4 files) use at most one builder plus a spawned verifier; only substantial multi-step work pays the full analyst->planner->builders->verifier->reflector pipeline. Reflection (memory update) is mandatory at every level, inline or spawned. Rationale: the E2E test showed the full pipeline costs ~10x inline execution for small artifacts (~168k subagent tokens for a 91-line README).
objects.reason: User asked for minimum token consumption per task; full-pipeline-by-default was the single largest waste. Verified 2026-07-02: this session's improvement batch ran inline at a small fraction of the E2E cost.

objects.fact: React 19 StrictMode failure pattern: the 'lazy guard' idiom in a component body (if (!started) { setStarted(true); void load(); }) fires setState synchronously during render, before mount, triggering an async side effect outside an effect boundary -> console error under StrictMode's double-invoke. Fix: move the guard into a useEffect (mount effect) instead of inline render logic. Project convention adopted: where the lazy-guard-in-render pattern is intentional and already effect-wrapped, suppress react-hooks/set-state-in-effect with a scoped eslint-disable-next-line + comment explaining why, rather than restructuring further. Two separate builders reproduced this same mistake independently this session (build:restyle-datos, build:restyle-flujo) before the orchestrator fixed it inline — treat this as a known trap when assigning React 19 StrictMode work to builders.
objects.context: Found while resolving PEND-007 (6 set-state-in-effect warnings) during the 2026-07-05 full-app redesign.

objects.fact: ORION agent-spawn reliability observed 2026-07-05: 3 of 10 spawns this session died mid-work (2 hit session/context limits, 1 got a connection-closed error) while leaving partial-but-real work on disk. Recovery protocol used successfully: diff the dead agent's claimed file ownership against actual `git status`/working-tree state, then either (a) finish the remaining delta inline in the orchestrator when small, or (b) re-spawn a narrowly-scoped agent targeting only the unfinished files. Do not blindly re-spawn the same broad task — it duplicates already-completed work and wastes tokens. New death mode observed 2026-07-28: a builder finished its work correctly on disk but returned an EMPTY/truncated report ('leaving the build running in background') without closing out its own verification. The orchestrator confirmed the artifact directly on disk and accepted it as done. Protocol: on a truncated/empty report, ALWAYS verify disk state before re-spawning — re-spawning here would have duplicated already-completed work. Separately, 2 of 15 spawns this session died from session limits (INFRA_DEATH) leaving no work at all in one case and complete work in the other — per RFC, infra-death does not inflate or deflate model-tier signal, record it as such rather than as a model failure.

objects.fact: Supabase migration pattern (error.code 42P01 / /does not exist|schema cache/) for all future migrations (003+): when an API route attempts to query a table that doesn't exist because a later migration hasn't run, the route detects error.code === '42P01' or error message contains /does not exist|schema cache/ and responds HTTP 503 {error:'MIGRATION_NNN_REQUIRED'}. The client's components/migration-notice.tsx catches 503 responses and displays a clear banner. This pattern was established for MIGRATION_002 (suppliers_quotes table) and must be reused for 003+ to gracefully degrade and inform users of pending migrations without breaking the app.

objects.fact: Claude Code built-in agent permission classifier enforces two hard blocks: (1) 'npm install' from external URLs (tarball CDN) is forbidden — agents cannot bypass package registry lock-in (see PEND-014, xlsx SheetJS CDN); (2) INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations against shared databases (like infrapilot-app's Supabase project) are forbidden without explicit user approval — agents may SELECT/read, but must ask before persisting data to shared resources (see PEND-002 write test). Both are safety gates; require manual user action or explicit write permission outside the agent sandbox.
objects.context: Discovered during this session (2026-07-05) when attempting to install fixed dependencies and test data writes. Complements KN-018 (agent spawn reliability + recovery protocol); these are the 'permission boundary' facts agents must respect.

objects.fact: SheetJS/xlsx round-trip discovery: the xlsx library silently DISCARDS formula cells {t:'n', f} if they carry NO pre-computed `v` value when the .xlsx binary is written. Workaround verified: every cell with f:'formula' MUST carry v:precalculated_numeric_result. lib/excel-export.ts implements this as function f(formula, value, fmt) that always bundles the precalculated value. Export pattern for modules: lib/<module>-export.ts exports crearLibroConFormulas(hojas, nombreArchivo) as a utility — clients can consume this for editable, formula-driven exports without relearning SheetJS internals. Pattern: every new module that exports Excel MUST use crearLibroConFormulas and populate all formula cells via f(formula, value).
objects.context: Discovered during ROAD-001 (hub + Excel exports). Verified via round-trip test: XLSX.write → XLSX.read confirms formulas persist only when v is present. This is a silent data-loss bug in the xlsx library if the precalculated value is omitted.
objects.source: session 2026-07-06, build:visual (dashboard hub with Excel export, opus)

objects.fact: Patrón: 'contratos cruzados en ola paralela'. Cuando un builder paralelo consume lo que otro produce en la misma ola (ej: ProfesionQuips importa crearLibroConFormulas de excel-export antes de que esa función esté completa), el consumidor deja el import y uso COMENTADOS con TODO si el proveedor no aterrizó al momento de su tsc. El orquestador descomenta los comentarios al cerrar la ola. Esta estrategia permite paralelismo máximo pero requiere diligencia post-ola: en ROAD-001 pasó con FileSpreadsheet (import faltante tras descomentar, detectado + arreglado inline, 1 fix trivial). Alternativa futura: secuenciar consumidor DESPUÉS de proveedor si la dependencia es fuerte y el paralelismo no compensa.
objects.context: Patrón validado en ROAD-001 (hub + Excel + quips). Costó 1 micro-fix (import olvidado) durante verificación. Documentar para equipos paralelos futuras.

objects.title: Ecosistema ORION v3: resiliencia a muertes, calibración aplicada, vault Obsidian
objects.description: 5 mejoras aplicadas 2026-07-06: (1) wave.json — manifiesto efímero de ola escrito antes de spawns paralelos (gitignored, se borra al completar; sesiones futuras recuperan olas muertas sin arqueología); (2) reflector atómico — orden dependency-safe en un solo write + auto-validación obligatoria antes de reportar (sessionCount==sessions.length); (3) calibración aplicada — analyst default haiku para objetivos claros, y modelOutcomes con subtipos build:visual|page|api|lib|infra para no diluir señal (infra-deaths no cuentan como señal de capacidad); (4) brief.md es el contexto primario del orquestador, state.json solo lecturas dirigidas; (5) tools/generate-vault.mjs — vista Obsidian unidireccional de la memoria (un .md por objeto con [[links]] + _INDEX), regenerada en cada close. POLÍTICA transversal nueva: los scripts deterministas los ejecuta el orquestador; los agentes solo hacen trabajo de juicio. EXPORT COMPLETO: tools/export-vault.mjs <destino> genera un vault externo con Sistema (estándar, RFCs, agents, skills, spec AMM) + todos los proyectos (permanent con prefijo PERM- para evitar colisión de links). El vault del usuario vive en C:/Users/Kalel/ORION-Vault — regenerarlo tras cada close si hubo cambios de memoria.
objects.reason: Derivadas del análisis medido de 16 sesiones: 5/28 spawns muertos por infraestructura (fallo #1), una corrupción de memoria por write parcial, calibración sin aplicar, y pedido del usuario de vista navegable de la memoria (Obsidian). objects.fact: proxy.ts redirected /sw.js and /manifest.webmanifest to /login (307) because neither path was in PUBLIC_PATHS. The build passed and each builder verified their own piece in isolation; the failure only surfaced running curl against the dev server. Fixed by adding both paths to PUBLIC_PATHS. Lesson: for any feature the browser requests without a session (PWA assets, webhooks, .well-known/*), always check the middleware/proxy matcher explicitly — a green build does not cover routes the middleware intercepts.
objects.context: Found building the PWA feature (ROAD-006) 2026-07-28; caught live by orion-verifier, not by build/tsc.

objects.fact: Ownership overlap ACROSS waves (distinct from KN-026's same-wave case): builders 'quips' and 'origen-de-presupuesto' both touched presupuestos/page.tsx in different waves; the second restructured the page and the first builder's quips survived only in the detail view, not the list view. Per-wave disjoint ownership does not protect a file that gets touched again in a LATER wave. Found by reviewing the prerendered HTML, not the build. When planning multi-wave work, track which files were touched in prior waves and re-verify their state after any later wave that restructures them.

objects.risk: The ampacity tables in lib/electrica/circuitos.ts (IEC/NEC-based) are only MEDIUM-confidence reference data, explicitly declared as advisory and overridable by parameter. If the app is used under a different local code (e.g. Chile's NCh Elec. 4/2003) the built-in values could be wrong for that jurisdiction.
objects.mitigation: Before presenting circuitos.ts results as authoritative engineering output in any jurisdiction other than IEC/NEC, validate the tables against the applicable local electrical code and expose them as clearly-labeled defaults the user can override.

objects.title: Nuevo agente ORION landing-prompter: produce el prompt, no la landing; 'sin inventar nada' implementado como procedimiento
objects.description: Agente opus creado en ~/.claude/agents/landing-prompter.md (espejo en runtime/agents/). Su output es el PROMPT con el que otro diseña la landing, no la landing misma. La restricción del dueño ('sin inventar nada') se implementó como checklist obligatorio, no como intención declarada: prohibido escribir el prompt antes de leer las fuentes reales; cada hecho debe llevar origen archivo:línea; marca real separada en voz alta de cualquier [PLACEHOLDER]; prohibidas las cifras sociales inventadas; toda duda queda como hueco explícito para el dueño, nunca relleno verosímil. Se le sembró memoria propia y nueva en ORION/memory/landings/ (POL-001, KN-001), validada VALID. Plantilla reutilizable para cualquier futuro agente ORION que produzca contenido de cara al público.
objects.reason: El dueño pidió un agente que aprenda y no invente nada; una prohibición declarada no basta para que un LLM no rellene huecos con verosimilitud — convertirla en procedimiento verificable (origen por línea, placeholder explícito) es lo que la hace cumplible run tras run.

objects.fact: La regla 'cliente afuera del negocio = tono de venta' no es universal. Para la landing de InfraPilot, landing-prompter decidió CONSERVAR el registro calmado del manifiesto estudio-diseno (DEC-010): quien mira esa landing es el mismo ingeniero que va a vivir horas dentro de la app, así que la calma ES el argumento de producto. La señal correcta para elegir registro no es 'público vs privado' sino qué necesita SENTIR quien mira la pantalla para comprar.
objects.context: Matiza DEC-010 (que no especificaba cuándo variar el registro fuera de la app). Encontrado escribiendo el prompt de landing de InfraPilot dentro del run de 8 proyectos de landing-prompter.

objects.fact: Copy de relleno que un asistente escribe 'para que la pantalla no se vea coja' sobrevive hasta producción y se convierte en una afirmación falsa del negocio (testimonios inventados, precios/productos que no existen en el catálogo real, horarios no verificados). Cualquier dato de relleno debe nacer marcado y bloqueante (placeholder explícito), nunca verosímil.
objects.context: Hallazgo transversal al investigar 8 proyectos para landing-prompter 2026-08-16: horario inventado confesado en comentario de código (mercaplaza pie.tsx:8-14), producto/precio inconsistente con el catálogo real (estanco-contable), y un testimonio + afirmaciones inventadas en infrapilot-app mismo (ver PEND-018).

objects.risk: Agentes que aprenden y escriben a su propia memoria (ej. landing-prompter) corrompen el archivo si se paralelizan compartiendo el mismo state.json/metrics.json. Comprobado en este run: 8 landing-prompter corriendo a la vez comparten ORION/memory/landings/state.json y se les prohibió escribir por esta razón.
objects.mitigation: Serializar la escritura de memoria (cola/lock, o que solo el orquestador escriba tras recolectar todos los veredictos) antes de paralelizar cualquier agente que persista aprendizaje; nunca dejar que N agentes paralelos escriban el mismo state.json/metrics.json directamente.

objects.fact: SI SE PUEDEN PROBAR LAS MIGRACIONES SQL EN ESTA MAQUINA, y el supuesto contrario tuvo a este proyecto trabado casi un mes. `npm i embedded-postgres` levanta un PostgreSQL real (18.4) en el scratchpad, se le aplican las migraciones y se corren asserts con node; NO hace falta psql, ni Supabase CLI, ni Docker. Aplicado a 003_organizations.sql esto permite validar ANTES de tocar la nube: (a) que corre sin error, (b) que es idempotente corriendola dos veces, (c) que las policies RLS con security-definer hacen lo que dicen, y (d) que el trigger de owner-bootstrap dispara. Lo que sigue necesitando al usuario es unicamente aplicarla en el SQL Editor del Supabase real: la verificacion deja de ser un acto de fe, pero el despliegue sigue siendo manual.
objects.context: Descubierto el 2026-08-24 por la capa transversal del cerebro ORION, no por trabajo nuevo: la prueba ya existia en OTRA memoria desde el 2026-07-29 (estanco-contable/KN-008, donde 001_rol_actual.sql se valido 37/37 con idempotencia y escalada bloqueada), es decir UN DIA despues de que infrapilot escribiera el supuesto contrario (RSK-001, 2026-07-28). Nadie las cruzo porque cada memoria vivia aislada. Es el caso que justifica el cerebro: no se aprendio nada nuevo, se dejo de perder lo ya aprendido.
